profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory (上海人工智能实验室) is a non-profit, government-affiliated research institution based in Shanghai. Its site describes it as focused on artificial intelligence research across areas including large models, embodied intelligence, trustworthy and safe AI, AI for Science, and foundational platforms. Since 2022 the laboratory has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten leading Chinese universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China, and Zhejiang University.

The laboratory's primary open-source large language model is InternLM, which the site promotes under the "书生" (Intern) brand family. At the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference science forum the laboratory announced ten collaborative AI-for-science results spanning life science, materials science, and deep-space astronomy, and released a scientific discovery platform called 书生·端砚, described as connecting science-oriented large models, specialist agents, experimental data, and embodied automation equipment to cover the full research workflow from hypothesis to experimental validation. The site also describes Intern-Robotics, a full-stack embodied intelligence engine aimed at addressing data, training, and deployment challenges for physical-world AI systems.

On AI safety the laboratory describes a framework it calls the "AI-45° balance law," which holds that AI safety and capability should develop in rough parity over time, and it outlines a causal-reasoning approach to trustworthy AGI proceeding through stages it terms broad alignment, interventionability, and reflective capacity. The held facts record no litigation or MCP server registrations associated with the organization.
